name: Per-serving with a minimum floor that DOES bind, no separate base fee
why: Kiddie Academy - Roland Park, 2026-07-25. Confirmed by the finance owner:
Billed $347.60 instead. The classifier chose INVOICE_BASE_FEE_PLUS_SERVINGS,
reading 'The minimum for 1 hour will be $250' as a base fee and stacking the
22 x $3 = $66 of servings on top: 250 + 66 = $316 subtotal.
A base fee ADDS; a minimum REPLACES. $250 is a floor, so the charge is the
GREATER of the floor and the per-serving total -- max(250, 66) = $250, then
Modelled as INVOICE_FIXED_PACKAGE with UNITS_INCLUDED_IN_BASE = 250/3 = the
servings the floor already pays for, which makes the engine compute the
greater of the two. The fractional value is correct, not a rounding error.
there a base fee ('$99 plus...') AND a floor were both stated and the floor
did NOT bind. 'plus' means add; 'minimum' alone means floor.
UNITS_INCLUDED_IN_BASE is deliberately NOT pinned: 250/3 is a repeating
fraction and any value at or above the 22 served yields the same $250. The
SUBTOTAL assertion is the real check -- it can only come out at 250 if the
model set the included count high enough for the floor to hold.
open_questions: The notes state two rates -- $3 'kiddie' and $4 'small'. The driver wrote
'22 green cups' without naming the size, so which rate applies is inferred.
It does not change this invoice (the floor binds either way, and 250/4 = 62.5
still exceeds 22), but the unused rate will trip the dead-terms gate, which
is the right outcome: a person should confirm the cup size.
